references.text: The first denial occurs just before this verse. Peter had just denied knowing Jesus, and now he is confronted by another person ([ref:Luk 22:57|Luke 22:57]).
Shortly after the second denial comes the third, where Peter again denies his relationship with Jesus, and the rooster crows as Jesus had predicted ([ref:Luk 22:59-60|Luke 22:59-60]).
Jesus predicted that Peter would deny him three times before the rooster crowed. This second denial is a fulfillment of that prophecy ([ref:Luk 22:34|Luke 22:34]).
Matthew's parallel account of Peter's second denial, where another servant girl recognizes him and Peter denies it with an oath ([ref:Matt 26:71-72|Matthew 26:71-72]).
Mark's parallel account where the servant girl again identifies Peter as one of Jesus' companions, and he denies it once more ([ref:Mark 14:69-70|Mark 14:69-70]).
John's parallel account of Peter's second denial, where he is asked if he is one of Jesus' disciples and answers in the negative ([ref:Joh 18:25|John 18:25]).
"Fear of man sets a trap." Peter's denial illustrates how fear of people can lead to falling, even for the most convinced believer ([ref:Ordsp 29:25|Proverbs 29:25]).
"Who are you that fears a mortal who will die?" Peter's fear of people in the high priest's courtyard stands in contrast to the call not to fear mortal humans ([ref:Jes 51:12|Isaiah 51:12]).
